item_arguments.argument: Defines the finite-horizon independent randomized block-gradient update, data, majorizers, and statuses.
Derives the block quadratic upper model from the block-gradient Lipschitz bound.
Proves the scalar absolute-value quadratic minimizer including both kinks.
Defines fixed-order exact block minimization, tie selection, budget, and failure status.
Proves the probability-dependent expected O(1/k) and smooth strongly-convex contraction bounds.
Uses lower semicontinuity and the continuous unique minimizer map to prove continuity of the value.
Constructs an explicit six-state cycle on a finite nonconvex indicator domain.
Derives nonzero-column soft thresholding and the unique zero-column rule.
Defines exact and certified-inexact randomized proximal coordinate updates and mapping-based stopping.
Proves block subgradient conditions and global optimality for finite coordinatewise minima.
Applies the actual OPT8 proximal existence theorem and the local descent model.
Refutes the broader penalty-independent R-only proximal rate with a one-step finite witness.
Refutes a curvature-only-in-the-penalty contraction claim with exact one-step values.
Proves optimal accumulation points and unique-minimizer convergence under the declared compactness and map hypotheses.
Proves existence, smooth-part curvature restriction, and uniform proximal coordinate error recurrence.
Shows the full continuum of optimal coefficients and the unique fitted vector for collinear columns.
Computes both possible randomized outcomes and the exact cyclic sweep on a rank-one quadratic.
Solves both ridge-regularized block quadratics and checks the residual and objective.
Calculates one exact cyclic Lasso sweep and all intermediate objective values.
Verifies the zero-column coordinate is uniquely zero for positive penalty.
Proves properness by finite induction, convexity by adding block inequalities, and epigraph closedness using local neighborhoods from the block epigraphs; no sequential-closure choice is used.

Local composite-curvature variant: shift F by mu norm-squared/2 for coercivity/attainment; use convex-f full-model bound and strong-F segment bound with t=mu/(Lmax+mu), then uniform-coordinate averaging and deterministic inexact convolution. Does not import the sharper smooth-part factor from Wright.
